Refactored the design to add a clean abstraction boundary.

What changed:
- Added [GraphView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/028_bipartite_graph/GraphView.java) as a minimal contract for graph access.
- Made [UndirectedGraph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/028_bipartite_graph/UndirectedGraph.java) implement that contract.
- Updated [BipartiteAnalyzer.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/028_bipartite_graph/BipartiteAnalyzer.java) to depend on `GraphView` instead of the concrete graph type.
- Kept [BipartiteGraph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/028_bipartite_graph/BipartiteGraph.java) as the thin entry point over graph construction plus analysis.

Why this is better:
- The analyzer now depends only on the behavior it needs, which is cleaner than coupling it to one implementation.
- `UndirectedGraph` stays a pure data/model type.
- The code is easier to extend if you later add another graph representation or a test double.
